title: SPDM 1.2 responder (DMTF DSP0274): device attestation in hardware with VERSION / CAPABILITIES / ALGORITHMS, DIGESTS, CERTIFICATE, CHALLENGE_AUTH and MEASUREMENTS, SHA3-384 transcripts on three SHA-3 engines and ML-DSA-44 / 65 / 87 signatures on an ML-DSA engine

fields.desc: CAPABILITIES CTExponent: the requester's timeout is 2^ct_exp microseconds (cover the ML-DSA signing time)
CMD.kg_start parameter set: 0 ML-DSA-44, 1 ML-DSA-65, 2 ML-DSA-87 (3 is refused with CMD_ERR)
CMD.kg_start seed: 0 the SEED registers, 1 the sideload port sl_seed (refused with CMD_ERR unless sl_valid)

regs.name: ASYM
regs.desc: ExtAsym entry of the ML-DSA key (RegistryID, reserved, AlgorithmID; little-endian as in the message)

fields.desc: matched against the requester's ExtAsym list in NEGOTIATE_ALGORITHMS and returned in ALGORITHMS
bytes of the chain in the store (0: slot 0 empty); at most 16384
bit i: measurement index i + 1 present
bit i: index i + 1 is part of the TCB measurement summary hash (CHALLENGE type 1)
bits 8i+7:8i: DMTFSpecMeasurementValueType of index i + 1 (the value is a 48-byte SHA3-384 digest)

regs.name: STORE
regs.desc: Store write: STORE0 = data word, STORE1 = {sel, address}, which commits it. sel 0: certificate chain word address (bytes 4a .. 4a + 3, little-endian); sel 1: measurement word 16 i + w (w = 0..11: digest bytes 4w .. 4w + 3 of index i + 1)

regs.name: SEED
regs.desc: KeyGen seed xi, eight write-only words (SEED0 = bytes 3..0); reads return 0. Write zeros after CMD.kg_start

fields.desc: generate the identity key (ML-DSA KeyGen of CFG.pset from the seed); refused with CMD_ERR while busy
stream the public key into PK; refused with CMD_ERR while busy or without a key
abort what runs (after an ML-DSA operation in progress), wipe the private key, the seed area and the nonce, end the connection

regs.name: PK
regs.desc: Public key word (PK0 = bytes 3..0, little-endian), PK1 = last flag; reading PK1 pops it. 1312 / 1952 / 2592 bytes

regs.name: RN
regs.desc: Random word (from a TRNG): eight per responder nonce, eight more per signature (rnd); the core takes them while it answers CHALLENGE and GET_MEASUREMENTS

fields.desc: a request, a command or a clr is in progress
connection: 0 none, 1 after VERSION, 2 after CAPABILITIES, 3 after ALGORITHMS
ErrorCode of the last ERROR response

features: SPDM 1.2 responder in hardware: GET_VERSION, GET_CAPABILITIES, NEGOTIATE_ALGORITHMS, GET_DIGESTS, GET_CERTIFICATE, CHALLENGE and GET_MEASUREMENTS are parsed, checked and answered without firmware; every other request code gets ERROR UnsupportedRequest. Error responses: InvalidRequest, UnexpectedRequest, UnsupportedRequest, ResponseTooLarge, VersionMismatch.

Post-quantum identity: ML-DSA-44, -65 or -87 (FIPS 204) signs CHALLENGE_AUTH and MEASUREMENTS; the key pair is generated inside from a 32-byte seed (a register or a sideload port, e.g. a DICE CDI from Root_of_Trust) and the private key never leaves the ML-DSA engine. The public key can be read for a certificate request.

Transcripts M1 and L1 hashed on the fly with SHA3-384 by two SHA3 engines; a third hashes the certificate chain for DIGESTS / CHALLENGE_AUTH and the measurement summary (TCB or all). The signed message is the DSP0274 1.2 combined SPDM prefix and context string followed by the transcript hash.

Byte-stream request / response port for a DOE mailbox or an MCTP binding; responses up to 4889 bytes are streamed as they are formed (the signature last), the requester's DataTransferSize is honoured (CERTIFICATE portions are clipped to it, larger responses get ResponseTooLarge).
Slot 0 certificate chain store of 16 KiB and four measurement indices (48-byte digests with DMTF value types) written through STORE.
notes: Message layouts follow the public DSP0274 1.2 text. SPDM 1.2 has no ML-DSA code point, so the key is negotiated through one ExtAsym entry (ASYM); the core is not claimed to be interoperable with a given requester stack.

The core needs no response buffer: header fields are formed from the request, digests come from the SHA3 engines, certificate and measurement bytes from the stores, the signature from the ML-DSA buffer.

Signing time: about 63k / 91k / 128k clocks per attempt of the ML-DSA rejection loop (4.25 / 5.1 / 3.85 attempts on average) for ML-DSA-44 / 65 / 87; set CFG.ct_exp so that the requester waits long enough (RESPOND_IF_READY is not implemented).
The stores and the CFG / MEAS registers are read while a request is answered: change them only while STATUS.busy = 0 and no request is in flight.

Not implemented: secured sessions (KEY_EXCHANGE, PSK_EXCHANGE, FINISH, secured messages; so IDE key programming by IDE_KM still needs a session from firmware), mutual authentication, slots 1-7, CHUNK_SEND / CHUNK_GET, SPDM 1.0 / 1.1 / 1.3, opaque data, raw bit-stream measurements, masking against power analysis.
sequence: Write the certificate chain (DSP0274 format: length, reserved, root hash, DER certificates) with STORE (sel 0) and CCLEN; write the measurement digests with STORE (sel 1), MTYPE and MEAS. Write ASYM with the ExtAsym value the requesters use.

Generate the key: CFG.pset (and kg_sel), SEED (or the sideload port), CMD.kg_start = 1; wait for IRQ_STATUS.KG_DONE, write zeros to SEED. For a certificate request, CMD.pk_open = 1 and read PK0 / PK1 until the last flag.

Keep RN supplied with random words (FLAGS.RN_FULL = 0: write the next word) while requests are answered; requests and responses use the rq_* / rs_* byte pins. IRQ_STATUS.RSP_DONE / RSP_ERR report each response.
CMD.clr = 1 ends the connection and wipes the key (generate a new one before the next CHALLENGE).
verification: Core: tb/SPDM_tb.sv runs 122 requests from scripts/spdm/gen_vec.py, an SPDM 1.2 responder model (scripts/spdm/spdm_ref.py) with the FIPS 204 model scripts/mldsa/mldsa_ref.py; every response is compared byte for byte, signatures of all three parameter sets included (and the generator checks each signature with ML-DSA Verify against the transcript). The requests cover every request code with every error it can get, both DataTransferSize limits, the measurement summary types, interleaved M1 / L1 transcripts, VCA restarts, the key commands and clr while a request is received, signed, sent and while KeyGen runs.

The core checker has its own SHA3-384 and keeps the transcripts as byte queues: it decides each request, forms every response byte but the signature (digests included), and checks the seed, M' and rnd in the ML-DSA buffer when KeyGen / Sign start, the wipes, the handshakes and the status outputs.
